metadata.title: TIMSS 2023: Insights into mathematics and science achievement in Ireland

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses TIMSS 2023 Ireland main-study samples at Fourth Class (primary) and Second Year (post-primary), drawn via a two-stage stratified school sampling design followed by random selection of classes within schools. The report reports weighted response rates and uses standard TIMSS scaling and uncertainty reporting (SEs and confidence intervals) consistent with complex survey estimation, but it does not explicitly name the student weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight procedures in the provided text. For the national mode effect study, paper and digital modes are administered to separate “bridge” samples under equivalent conditions, and the mode effect results are presented as mean comparisons with standard errors, again without explicit weight-variable names. No machine-learning model training is conducted; therefore, the report’s weighting discussion is primarily about producing population-representative achievement estimates and valid uncertainty quantification rather than about ML-specific weighting support.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a national descriptive/reporting document that presents TIMSS achievement scale results, benchmark attainment percentages, and curriculum coverage analyses rather than training predictive models on PV-based cognitive outcomes. Plausible values handling is therefore not applicable in the sense of a PV-combining procedure for an ML pipeline, and the report text provided does not document a specific missing-data handling strategy for PV estimation. Missing-data handling is not reported because the report focuses on official TIMSS scaling outputs and response-rate reporting rather than detailing imputation/deletion rules for item nonresponse.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic samples are the final weighted TIMSS 2023 Ireland participants at each grade level after: (i) teacher discretion exclusions for functional/intellectual disabilities and limited language proficiency, with guidance to exclude only students in Ireland for less than one year; (ii) parental withdrawals; and (iii) absences on the test day. For Fourth Class, 154 primary schools were selected and one ineligible school was replaced; the final dataset includes 153 primary schools, with 230 Fourth Class class groups and 4,750 Fourth Class pupils completing at least part of the test. For Second Year, 154 post-primary schools were selected and two were replaced; the final dataset includes 153 post-primary schools, with 246 Second Year class groups and 5,090 Second Year students completing at least part of the test. The report also notes that students with questionnaire data but no test data are excluded from questionnaire response-rate reporting.

data.outcome_summary: This TIMSS 2023 national report for Ireland summarizes mathematics and science achievement at two TIMSS grade levels: Fourth Class (Fourth Grade) and Second Year (Eighth Grade). It uses TIMSS’s matrix sampling and rotated booklet design, with achievement reported on TIMSS scales (centrepoint 500, SD 100) and uncertainty quantified via standard errors and confidence intervals. The report presents mean achievement, distributional indicators (percentiles), and International Benchmarks (Low/Intermediate/High/Advanced) as cumulative percentages of students meeting scale-score thresholds. It also reports performance by content and cognitive domains (Knowing/Applying/Reasoning; and content strands such as Number, Measurement & Geometry, Data; and Life/Physical/Earth Science) and includes curriculum coverage via Test-Curriculum Matching Analysis plus teacher-reported topic exposure. Finally, it includes a national mode effect study to assess paper-to-digital comparability, finding no statistically significant mode differences in mean scores.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is an official national reporting synthesis rather than an empirical ML study. As such, it does not train or compare machine-learning models, and it does not provide PV-combining or missing-data imputation/deletion procedures in the excerpted text. The extraction therefore leaves ML-specific fields empty and focuses on assessment design, sampling/response-rate reporting, and descriptive achievement outcomes.
